corrected_fields.summary: Chair Powell announced a 25bps rate cut to 4-4.25%, citing shifted balance of risks with increased downside employment risks and upside inflation risks. GDP growth moderated to ~1.5% in H1 2025. Unemployment edged up to 4.3% with payrolls slowing to 29k/month. Total PCE inflation was 2.7% and core PCE 2.9% through August. SEP median projections show GDP at 1.6% (2025) and 1.8% (2026), unemployment at 4.5% end-2025, and fed funds rate at 3.6% end-2025. Powell noted tariff effects on goods prices and that the Committee remains committed to dual mandate goals.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: The Fed's second consecutive 25bps cut signals a pivot toward addressing labor market weakening while inflation remains above target. The shift in balance of risks toward employment concerns marks a notable policy inflection. Markets will scrutinize the updated SEP projections and Powell's remarks on tariff pass-through for signals about the pace of further easing.
corrected_fields.macro_context: GDP growth slowed from 2.5% in 2024 to ~1.5% in H1 2025. Labor market has softened with payrolls well below breakeven. Inflation at 2.7-2.9% PCE remains above the 2% target. Tariff impacts beginning to show in goods prices. The dual mandate risks have shifted: near-term inflation risks tilted upward, employment risks tilted downward.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: FOMC press conference following the September 2025 rate decision. Key inputs for rates, FX, and equity markets. The 25bps cut and accompanying policy statement provide guidance on the near-term rate path. SEP dot plot updates and Powell Q&A on tariff effects are critical for front-end rates and risk asset positioning.
